title: Towards Distributed Cognition: Knowledge Gravity as a Foundation for Sovereign Neuro-Symbolic AI
content: The rapid adoption of Artificial Intelligence (AI) across public administrations, industry, education, and critical infrastructures is increasing demands for computational efficiency, transparency, sustainability, and regulatory compliance. While cloud-centric AI architectures have enabled major advances in machine learning, they face growing challenges related to data movement, latency, energy consumption, explainability, cybersecurity, and digital sovereignty. At the same time, European regulatory frameworks such as the European AI Act, GDPR, NIS2, the Data Act, and the Data Governance Act impose heterogeneous requirements concerning AI risk management, data protection, cybersecurity, data governance, accountability, and access to data. Current research addresses Edge Computing, Neuro-Symbolic AI, Knowledge Graphs, Explainable AI, and Sustainable AI largely as separate domains. This paper introduces SOFIA (Sovereign, Ontology-driven Framework for Intelligent Action), a conceptual knowledge-driven neuro-symbolic framework that integrates Edge-Cloud Continuum principles, Data Gravity, Knowledge Graphs, and Governance-by-Design mechanisms. SOFIA aims to define and operationalize the concept of Knowledge Gravity, extending compute-to-data approaches by considering the placement of semantic knowledge, reasoning capabilities, policies, and regulatory constraints closer to the points where decisions are generated across the continuum. Through the integration of machine learning, symbolic reasoning, and evolving Knowledge Graphs, the framework outlines how explainable and governance-aware intelligence could be deployed on resource-constrained edge devices while reducing reliance on centralized infrastructures. In this perspective, Knowledge Gravity is proposed as a conceptual orchestration principle for distributed cognition, where knowledge assets influence placement and governance decisions. To illustrate the proposed concepts, the paper introduces a preliminary mathematical formulation and a synthetic simulation based on hypothetical deployment scenarios. These examples are intended only to demonstrate the behavior of the proposed indicators and optimization perspective and do not constitute empirical validation of the framework. By framing knowledge placement, reasoning availability, governance requirements, and sovereignty constraints within a unified architectural perspective, SOFIA contributes a research agenda for distributed, explainable, and sustainable AI across the Edge-Cloud Continuum. The framework is presented as a conceptual foundation whose assumptions, metrics, and expected benefits require future validation in real-world deployments.
